title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The cote is Grothendieck's notes for his 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. The neighbouring 'pages' are typescript pages of SGA 7 Exp. IX (Néron models; pp. 186 and 188, printed numbers 504 and 506). The manuscript is written on the back of such scrap typescript, and the faint printed text on this sheet is that typescript showing through. The manuscript itself is a computation in the style of a 'filtered Poincaré lemma' carried out with simplicial resolutions.

Setting, as far as it can be read. X is a space (or topos) with a sheaf of rings S, and k is a base ring. Â^0_* is a simplicial S-algebra, apparently a completed divided-power polynomial-type simplicial algebra. It carries a decreasing filtration Fil^p, presumably by divided powers of the augmentation ideal, with Fil^p = everything for p ≤ 0. Two properties are recorded:
- (i) Fil^p(Â^0_*) is 'flasque' for all p ≥ 1. This seems to mean homotopically trivial or acyclic, possibly also sheaf-theoretically flasque.
- (ii) π_i(Â^0_*) = k for i = 0 and 0 otherwise. So Â^0_* is a simplicial resolution of k, as with PD envelopes of contractible simplicial polynomial algebras.

The simplicial de Rham complex is Â^*_* = Â^0_* ⊗_S Λ^* Ψ_*, where Ψ_* is a simplicial module of (PD) differentials. Grothendieck puts on it the Hodge-type filtration that extends the PD filtration of Â^0 and gives Ψ (degree 1) filtration 1:

  Fil^p A^i_* = Fil^{p-i}(Â^0_*) ⊗_S Λ^i Ψ_*.

He notes that this is stable under the (simplicial) differential, so it is a filtered complex of simplicial objects.

Homotopy computation. Using that Λ^iΨ_* behaves like a shift by i (décalage: Ψ_* has homotopy concentrated in degree 1), he gets

  π_ℓ(Fil^p A^i_*) = π_{ℓ-i}(Fil^{p-i} Â^0_*).

Hence:
- For i < p: the term is 'flasque' / homotopically trivial, by (i).
- For i ≥ p: Fil^{p-i} = Â^0, and Fil^p A^i_* = Â^0_* ⊗ Λ^iΨ_* has a single nonzero homotopy group, π_i ≅ k.

Conclusion. Regard Fil^p(A^*_*) as a (bi)simplicial resolution of Ŝ^{[p]} = Fil^p S, the p-th divided-power ideal. A spectral-sequence / acyclicity argument then gives

  H^i(Fil^p C^*_DR(X, Â^*_*)) ≅ H^i(X, S^{[p]}) for i ≤ p.

This is compatible with the unfiltered comparison H^i(C^*_DR(X, Â)) → H^i(X, S). He labels C^*_DR(X, Fil Â) ≃ Fil C^*_DR by definition and draws the commutative square.

An earlier attempt at the top, H^0(X,S) in degree 0 and H^i(X,S^+) in degree i ≠ 0, is crossed out.

Purpose. The aim is to compare the Hodge-filtered PD de Rham complex, computed via simplicial PD resolutions, with the cohomology of the divided-power filtration of S, in a range of degrees. This is a step toward a de Rham / crystalline comparison with filtrations.
errors: The case analysis of π_ℓ(Fil^p A^i_*) is heavily corrected. The surviving conditions ('0 si ... p≤i et ℓ≠i', 'k si p≤i=ℓ') omit the case i<p, where the term is claimed acyclic, so the displayed case split is incomplete or inconsistent as written.

The identity π_ℓ(Fil^{p-i}Â^0 ⊗_S Λ^iΨ_*) = π_{ℓ-i}(Fil^{p-i}Â^0) needs justification: an Eilenberg–Zilber/Künneth argument plus a décalage statement for Λ^i of a module with homotopy concentrated in degree 1 (Λ^i(M[1]) ≃ Γ^i(M)[i]). It also tacitly assumes Ψ has rank 1, or that the relevant divided powers of M are k. None of this is stated.
'Flasque' is used ambiguously, for sheaf-theoretic flasqueness versus homotopical acyclicity of Fil^p for p≥1. Both seem to be needed for the hypercohomology argument.

The restriction i ≤ p in the final isomorphism is asserted without the spectral sequence being written out (that attempt is crossed out). The crossed-out initial formula with S^+ was apparently abandoned as incorrect.

ideas.what: Simplicial PD-resolution Â^0_* of k with PD filtration whose positive pieces are acyclic, used to compute de Rham cohomology
ideas.modern_name: simplicial resolutions / derived (PD) de Rham complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (Complexe cotangent II, 1972, derived de Rham complex); Bhatt (2012, p-adic derived de Rham)

ideas.what: Hodge-type filtration Fil^p A^i = Fil^{p-i}(Â^0) ⊗ Λ^iΨ on the simplicial de Rham complex, mixing the PD filtration and form degree
ideas.modern_name: Hodge filtration on (PD/crystalline) de Rham complex; filtered Poincaré lemma
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (1968) contains related unfiltered ideas

ideas.what: Comparison H^i(Fil^p C_DR) ≅ H^i(X, Fil^p S = S^{[p]}) for i ≤ p via homotopy-group counting
ideas.modern_name: filtered de Rham / crystalline comparison (Fil^p of crystalline cohomology vs cohomology of J^{[p]})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot–Ogus; Bhatt (Hodge-completed derived de Rham ≃ crystalline)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1976 approach to the filtered PD de Rham complex via simplicial PD resolutions and a degree-range comparison with the cohomology of divided-power ideals. It anticipates in spirit the later derived/Hodge-completed de Rham comparisons, but is only sketched here.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck pursued a simplicial-resolution treatment of Hodge-filtered PD de Rham cohomology in 1976. This is of historical interest relative to Illusie's and Bhatt's derived de Rham theory, though the mathematics itself is not new.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a fairly routine homotopy-group computation within an unpublished 1976 lecture on the PD de Rham complex. The approach (simplicial PD resolution plus a filtered comparison) is historically notable as an early derived-de-Rham-style argument by Grothendieck. However, the results are standard by now and the page is fragmentary.
transcription_corrections: The faint printed text and the neighbouring 'pages' are SGA 7 Exp. IX typescript (pp. 186/188, printed 504/506) on the reverse/scrap side. They are not part of this manuscript's mathematics.
'filtration de régions' is likely a misreading; plausibly 'filtration de degrés' or similar, i.e. the filtration on Â_* extending that of Â^0 and giving Â^1 (Ψ) filtration 1.
'stable par l'application de l'A simpliciale' is probably 'stable par la différentielle de l'A simpliciale' or similar (stability under d).
The 'si p≤0' at the top refers to Fil^p(Â^0) = Â^0 for p ≤ 0, not to the π_i statement.
The final line is H^i(C^*_DR(X, Â_*^*)) → H^i(X,S), with a vertical arrow from H^i(Fil^p C_DR) and from H^i(X,S^{[p]}), forming a commutative square.
